rules.title: Prohibition on obtaining coordinator services
rules.requirement: A rental property owner, or its agent, representative, or subcontractor, may not receive, subscribe to, contract for, or exchange consideration for the services of a coordinator as defined by the act.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to a person directly or indirectly owning one or more rental residential dwelling units in New Jersey, or that owner's agent, representative, or subcontractor. A person holding a controlling interest in an owning entity and that entity count as a single rental property owner. Covered units are houses, apartments, accessory units, or other units intended as primary residences; inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities are excluded. A coordinator is a person operating algorithmic revenue management software or an algorithmic device that performs a coordinating function for a rental property owner, including an owner acting for its own benefit. An algorithmic device excludes a spreadsheet operating without artificial intelligence and requiring human analysis to process or calculate data, and a database using an algorithm only to query its stored unprocessed data. A coordinating function means: collecting competitively sensitive information from two or more rental property owners to analyze or process through an algorithm or automated process, including training, used to set or recommend rental prices, material lease terms, or occupancy levels; setting those prices, terms, or levels through an algorithm or automated process analyzing or processing another owner's competitively sensitive information, including training; or setting or recommending those prices, terms, or levels for two or more owners using the same or a substantially similar algorithm or automated process facilitating parallel pricing coordination. Competitively sensitive information is nonpublic information, including prices, supply, security deposits, ideal occupancy, lease termination, renewal dates, and other material lease terms; nonpublic means unavailable to the public at no cost, and a combination with public information remains nonpublic. Parallel pricing coordination means a tacit or express agreement between two or more rental property owners, including agreements between a coordinator and multiple owners, to raise, change, maintain, or manipulate leasing prices for reasonably interchangeable residential units, unless required by affordability controls. Tacit agreement means mutual consent without verbal or written communication and may, but need not, be demonstrated by a pattern of conduct. Coordinating functions exclude information provision, use, or collection solely for research, statistical analysis, or testing when the information is not used to set or recommend prices, material lease terms, fees, occupancy rates or levels, or other contract terms for current or future leases; developing estimated rent made publicly available at no cost; use of a real estate brokerage database available equally to subscribers that lists properties for rent or sale and neither sets or recommends rental prices, material lease terms, or occupancy rates or levels nor collects competitively sensitive information for those purposes; and lawful government setting or limiting of residential rents or sale prices through affordability controls. Such government entities are also excluded from coordinator status. Affordability controls are rent-price restrictions established under government programs, including the identified federal section 8 homeownership program, P.L.2004, c.140, the Fair Housing Act, New Jersey Housing and Mortgage Finance Agency programs, rent control or rent leveling ordinances, and other local, State, or federal housing programs.
rules.exemptions: The act's definitions exclude specified facilities, certain spreadsheets and databases, specified research and public rent estimates, qualifying brokerage databases, and lawful government affordability controls, as detailed in coverage.

rules.title: Prohibition on coordinator-facilitated anticompetitive agreements
rules.requirement: A coordinator may not facilitate a tacit or express agreement among rental property owners that restricts competition concerning residential dwelling units, including by performing a coordinating function.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to a coordinator facilitating a tacit or express agreement among rental property owners that restricts competition concerning New Jersey residential dwelling units. A coordinator is a person operating algorithmic revenue management software or an algorithmic device that performs a coordinating function for an owner, including an owner acting for its own benefit; lawful government entities setting or limiting residential rents or sale prices through affordability controls are excluded. An algorithmic device excludes a spreadsheet operating without artificial intelligence and requiring human analysis to process or calculate data, and a database using an algorithm only to query its stored unprocessed data. Rental property owners directly or indirectly own one or more rental residential units; a controlling-interest holder and its owning entity count as one owner. Residential dwelling units are houses, apartments, accessory units, or other units intended as primary residences in the State, excluding inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities. A coordinating function means collecting competitively sensitive information from two or more owners for algorithmic or automated analysis or processing, including training, used to set or recommend rental prices, material lease terms, or occupancy levels; setting those prices, terms, or levels through algorithmic or automated analysis or processing of another owner's competitively sensitive information, including training; or setting or recommending those prices, terms, or levels to two or more owners through the same or a substantially similar algorithm or automated process facilitating parallel pricing coordination. Competitively sensitive information is nonpublic information, including prices, supply, security deposits, ideal occupancy, lease termination, renewal dates, and other material lease terms. Information unavailable publicly at no cost is nonpublic, and mixtures with public information remain nonpublic. Parallel pricing coordination is a tacit or express agreement between two or more owners, including a coordinator and multiple owners, to raise, change, maintain, or manipulate leasing prices for reasonably interchangeable residential units, unless required by affordability controls. Tacit agreement is mutual consent without verbal or written communication; a pattern of conduct may, but need not, demonstrate it. Coordinating functions exclude information provision, use, or collection solely for research, statistical analysis, or testing when not used to set or recommend prices, material lease terms, fees, occupancy rates or levels, or other current or future lease contract terms; developing estimated rent publicly available at no cost; use of an equally available subscriber real estate brokerage database listing properties for rent or sale that neither sets or recommends rental prices, material lease terms, or occupancy rates or levels nor collects competitively sensitive information for those purposes; and lawful government setting or limiting of residential rents or sale prices through affordability controls. Affordability controls are government-program rent-price restrictions, including the identified federal section 8 homeownership program, P.L.2004, c.140, the Fair Housing Act, New Jersey Housing and Mortgage Finance Agency programs, rent control or rent leveling ordinances, and other local, State, or federal housing programs.
rules.exemptions: Definition-based exclusions and the affordability-controls qualification are preserved in coverage.

rules.title: Prohibition on parallel pricing coordination
rules.requirement: Two or more persons may not engage in or otherwise facilitate parallel pricing coordination as defined by the act, which excludes pricing action required by affordability controls.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to two or more persons engaging in or otherwise facilitating parallel pricing coordination. Person includes natural persons, corporations, partnerships, companies, trusts, and associations, unless context requires otherwise. Parallel pricing coordination is a tacit or express agreement between two or more rental property owners to raise, change, maintain, or manipulate leasing prices for reasonably interchangeable residential dwelling units, including agreements between a coordinator and multiple owners, unless required by affordability controls. Owners directly or indirectly own one or more rental residential dwelling units; a controlling-interest holder and the owning entity count as one owner. Covered units are houses, apartments, accessory units, or other units intended as primary residences in New Jersey; inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities are excluded. Tacit agreement means mutual consent without verbal or written communication and may, but need not, be demonstrated by a pattern of conduct. Affordability controls are government-program rent-price restrictions, including the identified federal section 8 homeownership program, P.L.2004, c.140, the Fair Housing Act, New Jersey Housing and Mortgage Finance Agency programs, rent control or rent leveling ordinances, and other local, State, or federal housing programs. This prohibition requires the defined agreement and the statutory participant counts; it is not a prohibition on every similar price or every use of software.
rules.exemptions: Pricing action required by affordability controls; facilities excluded from the residential dwelling unit definition.

rules.title: Prohibition on performing a coordinating function
rules.requirement: Any person is prohibited from performing a coordinating function as defined by the act, subject to its research, public rent estimate, brokerage database, and government affordability-control exclusions.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any person performing a coordinating function involving rental residential dwelling units in New Jersey. Person includes natural persons, corporations, partnerships, companies, trusts, and associations, unless context requires otherwise. A coordinating function means: collecting competitively sensitive information from two or more rental property owners for analysis or processing through an algorithm or automated process, including training, used to set or recommend rental prices, material lease terms, or occupancy levels; setting those prices, terms, or levels through an algorithm or automated process analyzing or processing another owner's competitively sensitive information, including training; or setting or recommending those prices, terms, or levels for two or more owners through the same or a substantially similar algorithm or automated process facilitating parallel pricing coordination. Owners directly or indirectly own one or more rental residential units; a controlling-interest holder and the owning entity count as one owner. Covered units are houses, apartments, accessory units, or other units intended as primary residences in the State; inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities are excluded. Competitively sensitive information is nonpublic information, including prices, supply, security deposits, ideal occupancy, lease termination, renewal dates, and other material lease terms; information unavailable publicly at no cost is nonpublic, and combinations with public information remain nonpublic. Parallel pricing coordination is a tacit or express agreement between two or more owners, including a coordinator and multiple owners, to raise, change, maintain, or manipulate leasing prices for reasonably interchangeable residential units, unless required by affordability controls. Tacit agreement is mutual consent without verbal or written communication and may, but need not, be demonstrated by a pattern of conduct. Affordability controls are government-program rent-price restrictions, including the identified federal section 8 homeownership program, P.L.2004, c.140, the Fair Housing Act, New Jersey Housing and Mortgage Finance Agency programs, rent control or rent leveling ordinances, and other local, State, or federal housing programs.

rules.title: Attorney General complaint intake website
rules.requirement: The Attorney General must establish a location on the Department of Law and Public Safety's official website to receive complaints alleging violations or suspected violations of the act. Establishing or maintaining such a location for New Jersey Antitrust Act complaints satisfies this requirement.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to the New Jersey Attorney General's administration of complaint intake for alleged violations or suspected violations of this act. The duty may be satisfied by establishing or maintaining an official Department of Law and Public Safety website location for complaints alleging violations or suspected violations of the New Jersey Antitrust Act.
rules.quoted_span:
7.    The Attorney General shall establish, on the

which requirement may be satisfied by establishing or maintaining such a

review.issue: The source identifies an enacted public law approved July 20, 2026, rather than a pending bill. Approval is distinct from the delayed effective date.
The effective date is calculated as July 1, 2027: the first day of the twelfth month next following the July 20, 2026 enactment. These duties are therefore not yet effective as of October 1, 2026.

9.    This act shall take effect on the first day of

review.issue: Section 5 preserves application of New Jersey Antitrust Act sections 6–17 to section 4 violations, but their operative text is absent. Specific penalties, remedies, standing, limits, and per-violation counting cannot be extracted from this source alone.
review.quoted_span:
5.    The provisions of this act shall not be construed

c.73 (C.56:9-6 through 9-17) to a violation of section 4 of this act.

review.issue: The act supplements existing law and does not authorize already unlawful conduct. The scope of any preexisting prohibition requires review of the referenced laws; the delayed effective date does not establish that the conduct is currently lawful.
